=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- changelog.d/6222-review-command-isolation.md:2 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The fragment asserts "The `audit-plans` command and its consumer template are synchronized" but the root `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` still carries the OLD wording ("`/implement-plan-claude` projects (in-progress") while the template at `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` carries the NEW wording ("legacy `/implement-plan-claude` projects still in flight... New `/implement-plan-claude` invocations dispatch the orchestrator"). The two files are not byte-identical — they diverge on lines 1, 29, 32, 103, 126, and 127. The changelog fragment claims a state that does not exist at the current HEAD.
  WHY: Operators reading this changelog entry would believe the parity issue from PR #6135 is resolved. Running the audit-plans command interactively still shows stale pre-retirement language. The `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py` parity test would fail against the current branch, blocking CI.
- Requirement: "synchronize `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` with `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` and run the existing `test_template_parity` regression test" (from linked issue #6222, Suggested fix section)
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md`
  Evidence of absence: The root copy at `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` uses the pre-retirement language ("and `/implement-plan-claude` projects (in-progress...", "in-flight `/implement-plan-claude` work", "/implement-plan-claude (in-session)", "/implement-plan-claude (Claude implements it in-session)") on lines 1, 29, 32, 103, 126, and 127. The template at `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` already carries the updated post-retirement language ("and legacy `/implement-plan-claude` projects still in flight... New `/implement-plan-claude` invocations dispatch the orchestrator" on line 1, "legacy `/implement-plan-claude` projects" on line 29, "legacy in-flight `/implement-plan-claude` work" on line 32, "Claude-engine orchestrator hand-off" on lines 103 and 126, "legacy `/implement-plan-claude` project" on line 127). The PR diff shows these changes were authored but they did not reach the current HEAD. The working tree carries the OLD root text. The parity test at `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:29-30` requires byte-for-byte parity and would fail.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:8225 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: In test_review_isolation_traverses_only_allowed_github_directories, the test fixture never creates host / ".claude/commands" or host / ".claude/commands/audit-plans.md" during setup (lines 8188-8196). When this assertion executes, Path.read_text() fails with FileNotFoundError.
  WHY: During setup of the temporary host directory (lines 8188-8196), only host / ".claude/hooks" and its files are created. Neither host / ".claude/commands" nor host / ".claude/commands/audit-plans.md" exists. Calling read_text() on the non-existent file causes pytest to fail unconditionally with FileNotFoundError. The setup must populate host / ".claude/commands/audit-plans.md" with "operator command\n" (matching how WORKFLOW.md is set up) or the test must assert that the file does not exist.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py: lines 8188-8198 (test fixture setup); intended assertion block at lines 8220-8227 in the PR diff | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR diff shows a new test assertion block (`(source / ".claude/commands").mkdir()` → `(source / ".claude/commands/audit-plans.md").write_text("untrusted\n")` → `assert result.returncode != 0` → `assert "reason=unsafe_directory" in result.stderr` → `assert (host / ".claude/commands/audit-plans.md").read_text() == "operator command\n"`) is supposed to be inserted between line 8219 (`assert (host / "scripts/claude_settings.json.tmpl").read_text() == "after\n"`) and line 8220 (`(source / ".github/ai/WORKFLOW.md").write_text("untrusted\n")`). The fixture at lines 8188-8198 only creates `.claude/hooks/` and writes `gh_api_write_guard.py` / `other.py`; it never creates `.claude/commands/` or `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md`. The actual file content I read shows the assertion block was NOT applied: line 8219 is followed directly by line 8220 with no new block between them. The linked issue explicitly required "Keep the trusted helper's directory rejection intact; do not rely on a PR-head allowlist edit to make an isolated editor transfer an operator-facing command," and the missing assertion is the regression test that proves the rejection still works for the `.claude/commands/` directory.
  WHY: Even if the assertion block were applied, the host-side `Path.read_text()` would raise `FileNotFoundError` because the fixture does not create `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` in the host. The test would error before it could assert the "operator command\n" content. As currently on disk, the test regression for `.claude/commands/` directory rejection simply does not exist, so the only enforcement that `.claude/commands/` cannot be transferred is the absence of any test for that path.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md: line 1; line 29; line 32; line 103; lines 126-127 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root command file and the consumer template file are not byte-identical. Root line 1 reads "and `/implement-plan-claude` projects (in-progress..." while the template line 1 reads "and legacy `/implement-plan-claude` projects still in flight (in-progress... New `/implement-plan-claude` invocations dispatch the orchestrator rather than creating in-session projects." Root line 29 names only "/implement-plan-ai" as the orchestrator runner; the template names "/implement-plan-ai or the new /implement-plan-claude". Root line 32 still says "Enumerate in-flight /implement-plan-claude work" while the template says "Enumerate legacy in-flight /implement-plan-claude work". Root line 103 references "/implement-plan-claude (in-session)" while the template references "/implement-plan-claude (Claude-engine orchestrator hand-off)". Root lines 126-127 still describe the old in-session Claude implementation path. The PR diff shows the intended synchronized text but those changes were not actually applied to the root file.
  WHY: The linked issue states "synchronize `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` with `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` and run the existing `test_template_parity` regression test." `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:29-30` enforces byte-for-byte parity; the divergence will fail that test in CI. Operators running `/audit-plans` interactively get stale instructions that misdescribe the new orchestrator-routed `/implement-plan-claude` behavior, which is the exact confusion the linked issue's "AI Issue Summary" asked us to prevent.
- Requirement: "synchronize `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` with `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` and run the existing `test_template_parity` regression test" (linked issue #6222, "Suggested fix" section)
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/audit-plans.md
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff includes hunk hunks at lines 1, 26-35, 100-106, and 123-130 showing the intended replacement text. The actual file on disk still contains the OLD wording on lines 1, 29, 32, 103, 126-127. `tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:29-30` requires byte-for-byte parity and will fail until the two files match.
  SEVERITY: critical
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  Expected change site: tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py, in the test that exercises transfer rejection for unapproved directories
